examples.ko: 이 가게는 모든 메뉴 가격이 균일해요.
examples.en: At this shop, every menu item is the same price.

examples.ko: 반죽을 균일하게 펴야 빵이 고르게 익어요.
examples.en: You have to spread the dough evenly for the bread to bake evenly.

examples.ko: 학생들의 점수가 균일하지 않아서 반을 나눴어요.
examples.en: The students' scores weren't uniform, so we split the class.
I chose wallpaper with an even color.
The items are uniform in size, so they're easy to pack.
I bought a pot that spreads heat evenly.

explain: '고르다'와 비슷하지만 크기, 두께, 가격, 품질처럼 비교할 수 있는 것이 모두 같을 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '고르다'가 더 자연스러워요. 가격을 같게 받는 '균일가'도 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: We sell all items at a uniform price.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 뒤의 말을 꾸미고, 가격이 모두 같을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In this form it modifies the noun; often used when all prices are the same.

phrases.en: The thickness is not uniform.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 크기나 두께가 서로 다르다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say that size or thickness varies.

phrases.en: This factory's product quality is consistent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품마다 품질 차이가 거의 없다는 뜻으로 공장이나 상품 설명에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means there is almost no quality difference between products; used for factories and product descriptions.

explain_en: It is similar to '고르다' (even), but is used when things that can be compared, such as size, thickness, price or quality, are all the same. In everyday conversation, '고르다' sounds more natural. Also learn '균일가', meaning one fixed price for everything.

examples.en: House prices are showing a sharp upward trend these days.
Gas prices turned sharply upward, so the burden is big.
There was news that the sharp rise has lost some steam.
The sharp rise in vegetable prices is due to the rainy season.
I was startled by the surge and sold my stocks.
It's in a sharp rise now, so I'm afraid to buy.

explain: '급등세를 보이다/타다/이어가다'처럼 값이 빠르게 오르는 흐름을 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '급락세'이고, 뉴스에서 집값, 주가, 환율 이야기에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: Gold prices are surging these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값이 빠르게 오르는 흐름에 올라탄 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of riding a fast upward trend in prices.

phrases.example: 환율이 이번 주에도 급등세를 이어가고 있어요.
phrases.en: The exchange rate continues its sharp rise this week too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급하게 오르는 일이 계속될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sharp rise keeps going.

phrases.en: The sharp rise in housing prices finally slowed down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 오르던 흐름이 약해지거나 멈췄을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a fast rise weakens or stops.

explain_en: It describes a fast upward trend, as in '급등세를 보이다/타다/이어가다'. The opposite is '급락세', and it appears in news about house prices, stocks and exchange rates.

examples.ko: 이 종목은 급상승 뒤에 급락하는 일이 잦아요.
examples.en: This stock often plunges after a sharp rise.

examples.ko: 코인 가격이 급락해서 손해를 본 친구가 많아요.
examples.en: Crypto prices plunged, and many friends lost money.
The stock price suddenly plunged yesterday.
In winter, the temperature often drops sharply.
When popularity plunges, advertising also decreases.

examples.ko: 급락한 가격에 물건을 사려는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people want to buy at the sharply reduced price.

explain: '떨어지다'보다 훨씬 갑작스럽고 크게 내려갈 때 써요. 주가, 가격, 기온, 인기에 쓰고 반대말은 '급등하다'예요.

phrases.en: The stock price plunged yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급락하다'의 과거 해요체로, 이미 일어난 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past polite form, used for something that already happened.

phrases.en: The temperature is plunging these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 빠르게 떨어지는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is falling fast right now.

phrases.en: When the rumor spread, the stock price crashed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 값이 아주 크게 한꺼번에 떨어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for a very big, all-at-once fall in value.

explain_en: It is much more sudden and large than '떨어지다' (to fall). It is used for stock prices, prices, temperature and popularity, and the opposite is '급등하다'.

examples.en: I learned that paying taxes is a duty of the people.
I file my tax return every May.

examples.ko: 성실하게 납세하는 사람에게 혜택을 주는 나라도 있어요.
examples.en: Some countries give benefits to people who faithfully pay their taxes.

examples.ko: 외국인도 한국에서 돈을 벌면 납세 의무가 생겨요.
examples.en: Foreigners also have a duty to pay taxes if they earn money in Korea.
I needed a tax payment certificate, so I went to the tax office.

examples.ko: 납세자의 날에는 세금을 성실히 낸 사람들에게 상을 줘요.
examples.en: On Taxpayers' Day, awards are given to people who paid their taxes faithfully.

explain: 일상에서는 '세금을 내다'라고 하고, '납세'는 '납세자', '납세 의무', '납세 증명서'처럼 딱딱한 말 속에서 자주 만나요. 비슷한 '납부'는 세금뿐 아니라 요금이나 보험료를 낼 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 납세자는 세금을 정해진 날짜까지 내야 해요.
phrases.en: Taxpayers must pay taxes by the set date.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 내는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who pays taxes.

phrases.en: Citizens have a duty to pay taxes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법에서 정한 세금을 낼 의무를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The legal duty to pay taxes.

phrases.en: I pay taxes every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '납세'보다 일상에서 편하게 쓰는 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday way to say the same thing as '납세'.

explain_en: In daily life people say '세금을 내다', while '납세' appears in formal compounds such as '납세자', '납세 의무' and '납세 증명서'. The similar word '납부' is also used for paying bills or insurance premiums, not just taxes.

examples.ko: 우리나라 소득세는 누진세 방식이라 많이 벌수록 세율이 높아져요.
examples.en: Income tax in our country is progressive, so the more you earn, the higher the rate.

examples.ko: 누진세가 너무 높다고 불만인 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people complain that the progressive tax is too high.

examples.ko: 누진세 덕분에 소득 차이가 조금 줄어든다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the income gap narrows a little thanks to progressive taxation.
There was talk on the news about changing the progressive tax.

examples.ko: 저는 누진세에 대해 더 알고 싶어서 책을 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I borrowed a book because I wanted to learn more about progressive taxes.

examples.ko: 월급이 오르면 누진세 때문에 세금도 더 늘어요.
examples.en: When your salary goes up, your taxes rise even more because of the progressive tax.

explain: 전기 요금처럼 쓸수록 단가가 올라가는 방식은 '누진세'가 아니라 '누진제'라고 해요. 발음이 비슷해서 헷갈리지만 '세'는 세금, '제'는 제도예요.

phrases.example: 소득이 많으면 누진세를 더 많이 내요.
phrases.en: If you earn more, you pay more progressive tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 낸다고 할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for paying this tax.

phrases.en: Progressive tax applies to this income.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 소득이나 경우에 이 세금 방식을 따른다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means this tax system is applied to a certain income or case.

phrases.en: The progressive tax rate is high, so it's a heavy burden.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소득이 늘수록 올라가는 세금 비율을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the tax rate that goes up as income rises.

explain_en: A system where the unit price rises the more you use, like electricity rates, is called '누진제', not '누진세'. They sound alike, but '세' means tax and '제' means system.

examples.en: The company announced a wage freeze this year.
Even as prices rose, the bus fare was frozen.
Employees were disappointed by the pay freeze.

examples.ko: 은행 계좌 동결 소식에 사람들이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: People were shocked by the news of the account freeze.

examples.ko: 금리 동결이 시장에 어떤 영향을 줄까요?
examples.en: How will the interest rate freeze affect the market?

examples.ko: 등록금 동결 소식을 듣고 학생들이 안심했어요.
examples.en: Students were relieved to hear the tuition freeze news.

explain: 물가, 월급, 요금처럼 오르내릴 수 있는 것을 그대로 두는 일에 써요. 계좌나 재산을 못 쓰게 묶어 두는 일에도 써요. '동결하다'와 짝으로 외워 두세요.

phrases.en: A wage freeze was decided this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 월급을 올리지 않기로 할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a company decides not to raise pay.

phrases.en: News came out that subway fares will be frozen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교통비나 전기 요금 같은 값을 그대로 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when fares or utility rates are kept the same.

phrases.en: The police requested a freeze on that account.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 쓰지 못하도록 계좌를 묶어 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an account is locked so the money cannot be used.

explain_en: Used when something that could rise or fall, such as prices, pay, or fares, is held where it is. It also covers locking an account or assets so they can't be used. Learn it together with '동결하다'.

examples.en: This shop buys and sells used cars.

examples.ko: 집을 매매할 때는 계약서를 꼼꼼히 봐야 해요.
examples.en: When you buy or sell a house, you need to read the contract carefully.
He made money trading stocks.
A real estate agent helps people buy and sell land.

examples.ko: 허가 없이 동물을 매매하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not trade animals without a permit.

examples.ko: 요즘은 인터넷으로 물건을 매매하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days many people buy and sell things online.

explain: 일상에서는 '사고팔다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '매매하다'는 집, 땅, 차, 주식처럼 큰 거래에서 써요. '부동산 매매', '중고차 매매'처럼 명사 '매매'로 쓰는 일이 더 많아요.

phrases.en: I wrote a real estate sales contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매매'는 명사로 집과 땅 거래에 가장 자주 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun '매매' is most often used for house and land deals.

phrases.example: 이 땅은 자유롭게 매매할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This land can be freely bought and sold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거래가 허락되는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whether a deal is allowed.

phrases.en: People buy and sell goods at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '사고팔다'를 더 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech '사고팔다' is more natural.

explain_en: In daily life people say 사고팔다 more often; 매매하다 is for bigger deals like houses, land, cars, and stocks. The noun 매매 is even more common, as in '부동산 매매' (real estate sales) and '중고차 매매' (used car trade).

en: item or property for sale; listing

examples.ko: 이 동네는 나온 매물 자체가 별로 없어요.
examples.en: There are hardly any listings at all in this neighborhood.

examples.ko: 중고 사이트에서 마음에 드는 매물을 찾았어요.
examples.en: I found a listing I like on a secondhand site.
Good listings sell as soon as they go up.

examples.ko: 그 차는 매물로 나온 지 일주일 됐어요.
examples.en: That car has been up for sale for a week.

examples.ko: 매물 사진과 실제 모습이 너무 달라서 실망했어요.
examples.en: The listing photos and the real thing were so different that I was disappointed.

examples.ko: 요즘 전세 매물이 부족해서 집 구하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Jeonse listings are scarce these days, so finding a home is hard.

explain: 중고 거래와 집 구하기에서 자주 들려요. '부동산 매물', '매물이 나오다', '매물이 없다'처럼 써요. 사려는 사람은 '매물을 찾다', 파는 사람은 '매물로 내놓다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I heard a good listing came out near here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔려고 내놓은 집이나 물건이 새로 생겼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a new house or item is put up for sale.

phrases.example: 요즘 작은 집 매물을 찾고 있어요.
phrases.en: These days I'm looking for small houses for sale.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사려는 사람이 쓰는 말이에요. 집이나 중고 물건을 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said by a buyer looking for a house or used item.

phrases.en: I put my old car up for sale.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파는 사람이 쓰는 말이에요. 물건을 팔려고 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said by a seller when putting something up for sale.

explain_en: You hear this a lot in secondhand trading and house hunting, as in '부동산 매물', '매물이 나오다', and '매물이 없다'. A buyer says '매물을 찾다', and a seller says '매물로 내놓다'.

en: to be changed; to be fluctuated

examples.en: Exchange rates change every day.

examples.ko: 시험 일정이 변동되면 바로 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: If the exam schedule changes, I'll let you know right away.
I hope prices don't fluctuate much.

examples.ko: 비행기 표 값은 시기에 따라 변동돼서 미리 사는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Flight ticket prices fluctuate by season, so it's better to buy early.
I saw a notice saying the bus route will change.

examples.ko: 날씨에 따라 가격이 변동될 수 있어요.
examples.en: The price may change depending on the weather.

explain: 값, 수치, 일정이 상황에 따라 오르내리거나 달라질 때 써요. '바뀌다'보다 딱딱해서 환율, 물가, 일정 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요. 안내문에서 '변동 가능'이라고 쓰면 확정이 아니라는 표시예요.

phrases.en: If there is any change in the schedule, please contact me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '변동'과 '있다'를 같이 써서 안내문에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Noun '변동' plus '있다', common in notices.

phrases.en: The time may change.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확정이 아니라는 뜻으로 안내할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices to say something is not final.

phrases.en: Tomorrow's schedule has changed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변동되다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than '변동되다' and common in daily talk.

explain_en: Use it when prices, figures, or schedules move up and down or shift depending on circumstances. It is stiffer than 바뀌다 and often pairs with exchange rates, prices, and schedules. '변동 가능' on a notice means it is not final.

en: being non-taxable; being tax-free; being tax-exempt

examples.ko: 이 상품은 이자가 비과세라서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This product is popular because the interest is tax-free.

examples.ko: 비과세 혜택을 받으려면 조건을 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: You need to check the conditions to get the tax-exempt benefit.
I wonder which items are non-taxable in the year-end tax settlement.
The interest on this account is treated as tax-free.
I'm planning to sign up for a tax-free savings account.
Please tell me what the tax-exempt limit is.

explain: 반대말은 '과세'예요. '비과세 혜택', '비과세 상품'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙이거나 '비과세로 처리되다'처럼 써요. '면세'는 '면세점'처럼 물건에 붙는 세금을 면제할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This account has a tax-free benefit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 내지 않아도 되는 이익을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the benefit of not having to pay tax.

phrases.en: I signed up for a tax-free product at the bank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금이 붙지 않는 금융 상품을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a financial product that is not taxed.

phrases.en: This money is treated as tax-free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 매기지 않는 것으로 정해질 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is decided to be exempt from tax.

explain_en: The opposite is '과세' (taxation). It is used before nouns, as in '비과세 혜택' and '비과세 상품', or in '비과세로 처리되다'. '면세' often appears in words like '면세점' (duty-free shop), where the tax on goods is waived.

examples.en: How much is the meeting room fee per hour?

examples.ko: 이 앱은 사용료를 내야 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to pay a fee to use this app.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 사용료가 싸지만 위치가 불편해요.
examples.en: The fee for this building is cheap, but the location is inconvenient.
You also have to pay the campsite fee in advance.
You only need to pay the usage fee every month.
They maintain the facility with the fees they receive.

explain: '사용료'는 쓴 만큼 내는 돈이고 '이용료'도 거의 같은 상황에 써요. 방이나 땅을 빌릴 때는 '임대료', 물건을 빌릴 때는 '대여료'라고 해요. '사용료를 내다', '사용료를 받다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.en: How much is the parking lot fee?
phrases.nuance_ko: '사용료'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 시설이나 서비스를 쓸 때 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 사용료. Often used for facilities or services.

phrases.en: I pay the usage fee every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 지불한다는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for paying the fee.

phrases.en: The fee for this place is expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요. '싸다'로 바꿔서 쓸 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about price. You can swap in 싸다 (cheap).

explain_en: 사용료 is money paid for what you use, and 이용료 fits almost the same situations. Renting a room or land is 임대료, and renting an item is 대여료. It pairs with '사용료를 내다' (to pay) and '사용료를 받다' (to charge).

en: to calculate; to compute; to estimate

examples.en: Insurance premiums are calculated differently depending on age.
The way taxes are calculated is complicated.

examples.ko: 피해 금액을 산정한 뒤에 보상을 시작할 거예요.
examples.en: We will start the compensation after we work out the amount of damage.
The monthly rent was set based on the floor area.

examples.ko: 점수를 어떻게 산정할지 먼저 정해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to decide first how to calculate the scores.

examples.ko: 이 요금은 사용량에 맞춰 산정하면 돼요.
examples.en: You can work out this fee according to the amount used.

explain: '계산하다'는 숫자를 더하고 곱하는 일 전반에 쓰고, 산정하다는 요금·세금·보험료·점수처럼 기준을 정해서 값을 매길 때 써요. '비용을 산정하다', '기준으로 산정하다'처럼 말해요. 대화보다 뉴스·계약서·공문에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I will work out the moving costs and let you know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기준을 정해 값을 매길 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for setting a value by a standard.

phrases.en: The fee is calculated according to usage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산정하다의 피동형으로, 값이 정해지는 방식을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used to explain how a value gets set.

phrases.en: Please check the calculation criteria first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공문이나 안내문에 자주 나오는 명사형 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun pairing common in official notices.

explain_en: '계산하다' covers adding and multiplying numbers in general, while '산정하다' is for setting a value by a standard, such as fees, taxes, insurance premiums or scores. Typical uses are '비용을 산정하다' and '기준으로 산정하다'. You see it more in news, contracts and official documents than in conversation.

examples.en: The tax rate went up a little this year.
Tax rates differ by country.

examples.ko: 세율이 낮은 나라로 회사를 옮기는 경우도 있어요.
examples.en: Some companies move to countries with low tax rates.
A high tax rate applies to this item.
The government announced it will lower the tax rate.

examples.ko: 세율을 알아야 정확한 세금을 계산할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You need to know the rate to calculate the exact tax.

explain: '세금'은 내는 돈이고 '세율'은 그 돈을 정하는 비율이에요. '소득세율', '부가가치세율'처럼 앞에 세금 이름을 붙여요. '세율이 오르다/내리다'와 '세율을 올리다/내리다'를 짝으로 외워 두세요.

phrases.en: The tax rate will go up next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세율'이 주어일 때는 '오르다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: When 세율 is the subject, use 오르다.

phrases.en: The government lowered the tax rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세율'이 목적어일 때는 '내리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: When 세율 is the object, use 내리다.

phrases.en: The income tax rate depends on income.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금 이름을 앞에 붙여 어떤 세금의 비율인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding a tax name in front says which tax rate you mean.

explain_en: '세금' is the money you pay and '세율' is the rate that decides it. Put the tax name in front, as in '소득세율'. Learn '세율이 오르다/내리다' together with '세율을 올리다/내리다'.

examples.en: Our country imports oil, so it is sensitive to fuel prices.

examples.ko: 한국은 이 과일의 주요 수입국 중 하나예요.
examples.en: Korea is one of the main importing countries of this fruit.
With more importing countries involved, the price went down a little.
It is safer if you increase the variety of importing countries.
I saw on the news which countries import rice.
The importing country raised taxes, so the price of the goods went up.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '수출국'이에요. 뉴스에서는 '주요 수입국', '최대 수입국'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Korea is a car exporting country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수입국'과 반대로, 물건을 파는 나라예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '수입국'; the country that sells goods.

phrases.example: 이 나라는 우리 회사 제품의 최대 수입국이에요.
phrases.en: This country is the biggest importer of our company's products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 회사에서 가장 많이 사는 나라를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news or business for the country that buys the most.

phrases.example: 이 제품은 수입국이 계속 늘어나고 있어요.
phrases.en: The number of countries importing this product keeps growing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 사 가는 나라가 많아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when more countries start buying a product.

explain_en: Its counterpart is '수출국' (exporting country). In the news it appears as '주요 수입국' (main importing country) or '최대 수입국' (largest importing country).
